q: 1. In a country road length in km is taken to a population of .............
explain: In road planning and density calculations, the population unit is typically considered per thousand to determine the road length required for a specific region.

q: 2. Economic survey of a proposed road project includes a detailed survey of .............
options: agricultural and industrial products available in the area
resources income to local bodies as toll tax
explain: An economic survey focuses on traffic potential. The Origin and Destination (O & D) survey is the most important for evaluating the economic utility and future traffic growth of a road.

q: 3. A precise survey is .............
explain: The final location survey is the most precise as it involves detailed staking out of the centerline and preparing detailed working drawings for construction.

q: 4. Mostly used road in Nepal is .............
explain: Due to the mountainous terrain and economic constraints, the majority of Nepal's rural road network consists of earthen (unpaved) tracks.

q: 5. In Bitumen Bound Macadam roads a Bituminous premix at the following temperature is applied .............
explain: Hot-mix bitumen must be heated to approximately 150°C to 160°C to ensure proper viscosity for mixing with aggregates.

q: 6. An effective way of conducting 'Origin and destination studies' to extract more information is .............
explain: Roadside interviews allow surveyors to ask detailed questions about purpose, frequency, and specific route, which other methods miss.

q: 7. An instrument used to study 'Spot Speeds' in traffic engineering is .............
explain: The enoscope (or mirror box) is a simple, inexpensive device used to measure the instantaneous speed of vehicles over a short distance.

q: 8. Centre line for an urban road of more than 4 lanes is .............
options: 3 m long broken line with a gap of 4.5 m in between lines
two thick parallel lines with a gap of 75 mm in between
explain: On multi-lane urban roads, a double solid white or yellow line is used to strictly prohibit crossing into opposing traffic lanes.

q: 9. The inventor of road making as a building science, was .............
explain: Pierre-Marie-Jérôme Trésaguet (1716–1796) is often credited with establishing the first scientific approach to road construction in France.

q: 10. The road foundation for modern highway construction, was developed by .............
explain: Thomas Telford and John Loudon McAdam both contributed essential modern principles: Telford emphasized heavy foundations, while McAdam focused on surface drainage and size-graded stone.

q: 11. Traffic engineering only includes
options: design and application of control devices
explain: Traffic engineering is a broad field covering the safe and efficient movement of people and goods through planning, design, and operations.

q: 12. At intersection of roads, the traffic volume study is carried out to ascertain the number of vehicles
explain: Directional counts are essential at intersections to design signal timings and dedicated turning lanes.

q: 13. Increase in traffic volume, due to increase in transport vehicles, is known as
explain: Normal growth accounts for the general increase in vehicle ownership and population over time, independent of a specific new road project.

q: 14. Volume of traffic which would immediately use a new road or an improved one when opened to traffic, is known
explain: Current traffic is the initial volume expected on day one, consisting of existing traffic diverted from other routes.

q: 15. Maximum number of passenger cars that can pass a given point on a road during one hour under the most ideal road way and traffic conditions, is known as
explain: Basic capacity is the theoretical maximum under 'ideal' conditions, assuming all vehicles travel at the same speed and minimum spacing.

q: 16. Maximum number of vehicles that can pass a given point on a lane during one hour without creating un-reasonable delay, is known as
explain: Practical capacity (or design capacity) is the volume that can be handled while maintaining a specific Level of Service (LOS) and acceptable delay.

q: 17. If brakes of vehicles are effective, the vehicle-running at 30 km/hour comes to a stop in
explain: Under standard braking conditions for a speed of 30 km/h, the average stopping distance required is approximately 10 meters.

q: 18. The head light of vehicles should be such that its lower beam illuminates objects at
explain: For safety, the dipped (lower) beam should reach at least 30 meters to provide sufficient reaction time at low urban speeds.

q: 19. In case of a multi-lane road, overtaking is generally permitted
options: from both sides right and left
explain: In countries that drive on the left (like Nepal/India), overtaking is legally performed from the right side for better visibility of oncoming traffic.

q: 20. At a road junction, 16 cross conflict points are severe, if
options: one is two-way road and other is one-way road
explain: A standard intersection of two two-way roads creates 24 conflict points, 16 of which are major 'crossing' conflicts.

q: 21. At a road junction, 7 cross conflict points are severe if
options: one is two-way road and other is one-way road
explain: Reducing one of the roads to one-way traffic significantly drops the number of severe crossing conflict points (to approximately 7).

q: 22. A road connecting two town is called a ............
explain: Highways are main roads designed for high-speed travel that typically connect major towns or cities.

q: 23. In Telford construction, the side portions were made up of only one layer of broken stones and leveled off to give a camber not greater than ............
explain: Thomas Telford utilized a standard cross-slope (camber) of 1 in 40 for the top surface of his road construction method.

q: 24. The camber, for the drainage of surface water, was first introduced by ............
explain: Pierre-Marie-Jérôme Trésaguet is credited with being the first to introduce the concept of camber to improve drainage in road construction.

q: 25. The unit cost of transportation (Au) on a section of the highway may roughly be calculated by ............
explain: The unit cost (Au) is generally expressed as the total cost (A) divided by the product of the number of vehicles (N) and the distance (L), hence A/NL.

q: 26. The traffic volume is equal to ............
explain: The fundamental traffic flow equation is q = k × v, where Flow (q) = Density (k) × Speed (v).

q: 27. The average number of vehicles per day passing on a section of the road during a particular year, is called ............
explain: Average Daily Traffic (ADT) is the total volume of traffic during a period (usually a year) divided by the number of days in that period.

q: 28. The volume of traffic, that would immediately use a new or an improved road when opened to traffic, is known as ............
explain: Current traffic is the existing traffic volume that diverts to a new facility immediately upon its opening.

q: 29. The increase in traffic constitutes the ............
explain: Future traffic volume accounts for normal growth, traffic generated by the new facility, and traffic from new land developments.

q: 30. The increase in traffic volume, due to the general increase in the number of transport vehicles, from year to year, is known as ............
explain: Normal traffic growth refers to the steady year-over-year increase in vehicle ownership and usage, independent of specific road improvements.

q: 31. Highway capacity is defined as the total number of vehicles ............
options: that can be accommodated on a unit length of the road
that can pass given point in a unit period of time
that can pass a given point in a specified period of time
explain: Capacity is the maximum hourly rate at which vehicles can reasonably be expected to traverse a point during a given time period.

q: 32. Highway density is defined as the total number of vehicles ............
options: that can be accommodated on a unit length of the road
that can pass a given point in a unit period of time
that can pass given point in a specified period of time
explain: Traffic density is the number of vehicles occupying a unit length of roadway (e.g., vehicles per kilometer) at a given instant.

q: 33. The practical capacity of highway is ............ that of possible capacity.
explain: Possible capacity is the maximum volume under ideal conditions, whereas practical capacity is what can be achieved under prevailing conditions without unreasonable delay.

q: 34. The design capacity is also known as ............
explain: Engineers design roads for 'Practical Capacity,' which ensures a desired level of service and safety for the users.

q: 35. The instantaneous speed of a vehicle as it passes a point in a highway is known as ............
explain: Spot speed is the speed of a vehicle at a specific point on the road, often measured using a radar gun or Enoscope.

q: 36. The average speed maintained by a vehicle over a particular stretch of road, while the vehicle is in motion, is known as ............
explain: Running speed is the speed calculated by dividing the distance by the time the vehicle was actually in motion (excluding stopped time).

q: 37. Traffic engineering deals with the ............
options: design and application of control devices
explain: Traffic engineering is a broad field covering the study of traffic behavior, planning, and the design of systems/devices to ensure safe and efficient movement.
